answers.rationale: The record shows trip-specific baggage choices rather than a fixed carry-on-only rule. For a booth trip, the poster tube, handouts, and suit make a checked bag the lower-risk practical choice while the laptop remains with the traveler.

This is driven by the stated no-car, midmorning-museum setup rather than a fixed hotel habit. The closest museum hotel minimizes first-morning transfer risk and makes a short family weekend easier; verify that its standard room actually accommodates all travelers before committing.

Late-morning sessions reduce the value of being physically attached to the venue, while family evenings make suite space and included breakfast materially useful. The history shows the user has made both proximity-first and space/breakfast-first choices depending on the trip, so no fixed preference is supported.

With activities split across two areas and no car, no single attraction-adjacent hotel clearly dominates. The roomier South Lake Union suite with breakfast better supports family mornings and downtime, provided transit or short rideshare access to Pike Place is reasonable. Prior choices vary between central paid-breakfast hotels and roomier breakfast-included options, not a fixed location rule.
